RCA (complete; investigation only)

OBSERVATION
Historical commit `c57057f41` added `--extra grounding-terraform` to `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` and not to `.github/workflows/test.yml`. The sweep lanes therefore installed `dev,reviewbot,ui` while the gating lane installed `dev,reviewbot,ui,grounding-terraform`. `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` existed and was edited in that same commit, but did not mention `grounding-terraform` or parse `--extra` lines.

HYPOTHESIS
The invariant in `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` covers shared gate delegation and many step signatures, but not the semantic install-extra set of test.yml sweep lanes versus the Verified/gating lane. Because no test extracts extras from both workflow families and compares them against an explicit allowed-divergence declaration, a commit can update the gating install line and the parity test together without failing.

CONFIRMATION
Confirmed by replaying the historical tree with `git show` only: at `c57057f41`, extracted extras from `_build-and-test.yml` were `['dev','grounding-terraform','reviewbot','ui']`; extracted extras from `test.yml` were `['agents','dev','reviewbot','ui']`; `grounding-terraform` appeared in the build workflow but not test.yml; and the parity test source neither mentioned `grounding-terraform` nor parsed `--extra`. I also ran the current parity file: it failed only on an unrelated POSIX-dash Makefile check, not on the still-visible extras dimension. This would have been disproven if the parity test had parsed both workflow install commands and required either equality or an explicit in-tree divergence record naming the extra/direction.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION
Add a data-driven workflow-extras invariant: extract extras per lane, compare gating and sweep sets, and allow only declared intentional divergences with actionable messages naming the extra and direction. Include an anti-vacuity regression that evaluates the `c57057f41` tree and fails.
